title: Structured data
content: Structured data is machine-readable markup that describes a page’s content using a shared vocabulary, such as Schema.org.

meta.why: Structured data can make the meaning of a page more explicit and support eligibility for applicable search features.
meta.example: A glossary uses DefinedTermSet for the collection and DefinedTerm for each visible definition.
meta.check: Validate the markup, compare it with the visible content, and keep names, URLs, descriptions, and dates consistent.
meta.limitation: Markup must describe the page accurately, Google requires no special schema for AI features, and valid markup does not guarantee a citation.
